summary: Only four supplied candidates directly apply a GNN-family method, message passing over relational graphs, to identifying fraudulent transactions. Ordered by headline reported score, while noting that the metrics are not fully comparable and that accuracy can be optimistic under fraud class imbalance: [V0049] uses LedgerGuard and reports accuracy 0.94; [V0052] uses GridWatch and reports F1 0.80; [V0051] uses ToxiBench and reports AUROC 0.73; [V0050] uses CellLife and reports MAE 0.66, an error metric rather than a higher-is-better detection score. No fifth supplied candidate meets both the requested method and topic criteria; [V0072] is appended only to satisfy the requested five-ID output and should be read as a fraud-topic representation-learning comparator, not direct GNN evidence.

claims.value: Representation Learning With Paired Positive And Negative Examples
